answers.answer: 1. Start with 25 money. 2. Begin with one active worker on the notepad and three inactive workers on the reserve spaces. 3. Draw eight Zoo cards, keep four and discard four. 4. Draw two Final Scoring cards. 5. Place side I of the five Action cards; Animals goes in slot 1 and the other four are randomly assigned to the other slots. 6. Starting Appeal counters are staggered by player order: first player 0, second 1, third 2, fourth 3.
answers.evidence: Setup, Personal setup B–F; Appeal counter stagger by turn order.

answers.answer: 1. In a four-player game, put the top four Base Conservation Project cards face up below the Association board; in two- or three-player games, put out the top three. 2. Only the two-player game blocks levels/spaces: cover the left level of the left base project, middle level of the middle project, right level of the right project, and the three spaces in the donation area's left column; both players are barred from them. 3. The summary specifies no special blocks for three or four players. 4. After everyone has selected starting hand cards, reveal all six display cards.
answers.evidence: Setup, global setup steps 5b–5c and personal setup G.

answers.answer: 1. Using the slot-4 card, remove it, shift cards from slots 1–3 one place right, and put the used card in slot 1. 2. Set action strength before performing it; each X-token spent adds +1 and is returned to supply. Newly gained X-tokens during the action cannot boost that same action. 3. You may hold at most five X-tokens. 4. Resolve an ‘after finishing’ effect only after the action is complete, including moving the Action cards.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: taking a turn; X-tokens; ‘After finishing’ effects.

answers.answer: 1. No: you may not take a regular action that plays zero animals or builds zero buildings. 2. If you cannot or do not want to perform one of the five actions, choose a card and take exactly one X-token instead; move that card to slot 1 and shift intervening cards right. Slot strength and upgrade side do not matter. 3. You cannot take this alternative if you already have five X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and X-token action: ‘You may not do nothing’; exactly 1 X-token; cannot with 5 held.

answers.answer: 1. A break token reaching its last space calls a break after the current turn. Ignore movement beyond the last space. 2. The player who moved it there gains one X-token for reaching the last space. 3. The triggering player completes the current turn before the break. 4. After the break, the token resets to the start space and normal clockwise play resumes with the next player.
answers.evidence: The Break track; Special Rules, ‘Break trigger from effects’.

answers.answer: 1. Cards I advances the Break token two spaces, then either draws from the deck according to its strength table (maximum three; discard if the table requires it) or, at strength 5+, snaps exactly one display card of any reputation, with no deck draw. 2. Cards II also advances the token two spaces, then draws from the deck and/or from display cards within reputation range in any order; its strength table applies. 3. Cards II snap works from strength 3 and takes exactly one card of any reputation, without a deck draw. 4. Reputation range limits only the Cards II draw-from-display option, not snapping. 5. Display cards taken during a turn are replenished only after the turn is complete. 6. Hand size is unlimited during play and checked only at breaks, when you discard to three cards, or five with the hand-limit university.
answers.evidence: CARDS action; Special Rules, ‘Display timing’ and ‘Hand size’.

answers.answer: 1. ‘Within reputation range’ means the display card in the folder matching your Reputation space and every lower-numbered folder. 2. Cards II is required to advance past reputation 9 and reach 10 or higher. 3. At reputation 15, each further reputation step gives one Appeal instead; the counter stays at 15. 4. You may not inspect the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: Reputation track and display; Cards action; Reputation spaces table.

answers.answer: 1. Build I constructs exactly one building of a size no greater than action strength; Build II may construct any number of different buildings whose total size is no greater than strength, but not two identical buildings in one action. 2. Pay two money per space, before placing each building. 3. The first building must have at least one space on a map border; later buildings must touch an existing building by an edge. 4. Build only on empty spaces and do not extend off-map, overlap, or cover water/rock. Restricted-icon spaces require Build II. 5. Each kiosk must be at least three spaces from every other kiosk. 6. Each pavilion immediately increases Appeal by one, once.
answers.evidence: BUILD action: side I, placement rules and side II.

answers.answer: 1. Build I permits standard enclosures, kiosk, pavilion and one Petting Zoo (size 3); each zoo may have at most one Petting Zoo. 2. Build II additionally permits one Reptile House and one Large Bird Aviary, size 5 each; each zoo may have at most one of each. The supply has four of each special enclosure for the four players. 3. Build cannot construct unique buildings; they enter through Sponsor cards. 4. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately gives seven Appeal; Build II is needed for restricted-icon spaces, though another effect can cover them.
answers.evidence: BUILD action building table, side II; Special Rules, ‘Full zoo map’.

answers.answer: 1. Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money and cards, may be used for later steps in that action; resolve items one at a time and pay each item before receiving its own benefits. 2. Thus previously gained money/bonuses may fund a later building, animal, or Association task if that action permits it. 3. Effects not designated ‘after finishing’ resolve immediately, even before the next item/animal; ‘after finishing’ effects wait until the entire action and Action-card movement are complete. 4. If effects are simultaneous, the owning player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, X-tokens and ‘After finishing’; Special Rules, simultaneous effects.

answers.answer: 1. Before playing each animal, meet all left-side conditions and pay its full printed cost; a matching-continent partner zoo reduces cost by three per matching continent icon on the card, so a double icon reduces it by six. Money gained from the animal's own effects comes later and cannot fund its cost. 2. Put a non-Petting-Zoo animal in an empty standard enclosure of at least its printed required size, then flip that whole enclosure to occupied; it normally houses one animal. Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo. 3. Eligible reptiles and some birds may instead use a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary; mark the card's indicated number of spaces with supply player tokens. Special enclosures never flip; animals may share if total capacity fits. 4. Meet any water/rock adjacency requirement. Count distinct adjacent terrain hexes, not edges; multiple touches of one hex count once. Requirements also apply when using a special enclosure. 5. Resolve normal play effects immediately (including before a later animal); defer ‘after finishing’ effects until the Animals action and card movement are complete.
answers.evidence: ANIMALS action, side I steps 1–5; Special-enclosure capacity.

answers.answer: 1. Animals II allows animals from the display within reputation range as well as from hand; pay an additional cost equal to the card's folder number. The display is not replenished until your turn ends. 2. At strength 5+, you may gain one reputation at the very beginning of the action, before selecting/playing animals, so the increased range applies. 3. Animals II permits animals whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon.
answers.evidence: ANIMALS action, side II.

answers.answer: 1. Only immediately when constructing a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary may you move corresponding eligible animals from standard enclosures into that newly built special enclosure; move all suitable animals that fit, choosing separately for each. 2. The new house must satisfy that animal's terrain adjacency requirements and have enough free capacity; mark the animal's indicated capacity with that many supply player tokens. 3. For each moved animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all its requirements, including terrain. If none does, flip the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size requirement; if none meets size, flip none. 4. This timing applies to construction through permitted bonuses too; this is relocation, not release.
answers.evidence: Moving existing animals into a newly built special enclosure; BUILD side II.

answers.answer: 1. Association task strengths are: reputation 2, partner zoo 3, university 4, conservation project work 5. 2. Association I performs exactly one task and needs at least one active worker. Association II performs one or more different tasks whose total strength value is no greater than the action strength; it still needs workers as applicable. 3. If you already have one worker on a task, repeating it requires placing two workers; if three of your workers are already there, you cannot repeat it before the break. 4. Other players' workers on the task do not matter.
answers.evidence: ASSOCIATION action, side I task rules and side II.

answers.answer: 1. Take partner zoos and universities from available tiles on the Association board, then place them on the lowest empty corresponding space of your zoo map and take any printed covered-space bonus immediately. 2. Do not take duplicate university kinds. Partner zoos must be from different continents; maximum four, with the third and fourth requiring Association II. 3. A partner zoo supplies its continent icon and reduces matching animal costs by three per matching continent icon. 4. Universities give their printed reputation and research icons; only the hand-limit university raises hand size from three to five. Other universities do not change it. The tiles are restocked at breaks except kinds already owned by every player; do not add duplicates.
answers.evidence: ASSOCIATION gain partner zoo/university; University tiles; Break procedure step 3.

answers.answer: 1. At Association strength 5, support a project already in play or play a Conservation Project from hand and support it immediately. Association II may instead play the new project from the display within reputation range, paying its folder number; no refill until turn end. 2. Choose a fulfilled condition with no player's token on that reward level; each level holds one token total across players. You normally may support each particular project only once, and may not support one that already has your token. 3. Place one player token taken from the seven on the left edge of your zoo map. Gain the depicted reward and activate the token's map bonus immediately, before or after the reward as you choose; recurring bonus income repeats each break. 4. A newly played card goes above the Association board, pushing others right. If over the player-count limit, discard the rightmost card and return its tokens to their owners' supplies (not to their map). Base projects below the board do not move or replenish.
answers.evidence: ASSOCIATION, Conservation project work; two separate support limits; Break-token/project rules.

answers.answer: 1. A Release into the Wild animal must match the depicted printed standard-enclosure size category, not an exact size: 2− accepts printed size 1 or 2, 3 accepts size 3, and 4+ accepts size 4 or 5. It must also match the depicted animal category. 2. First lose only that animal's printed Appeal, then discard it and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated Appeal, and earlier effects already earned. 3. Remove the animal's special-enclosure tokens if it could live in a special enclosure and the indicated tokens can be removed; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements, including terrain. If none qualifies, flip the smallest occupied enclosure meeting size alone; if none meets size, flip none. This applies to flock animals too. 4. Playing a new Release project grants one reputation; supporting one already in play does not.
answers.evidence: ASSOCIATION, ‘Release into the wild’ projects work differently.

answers.answer: 1. Sponsors I plays exactly one card from hand if strength is at least its level and its conditions are met. 2. Sponsors II may play one or more cards from hand or display within reputation range, paying each display card's folder number; strength plus one must be at least the sum of card levels. Upgrade-required conditions are allowed. 3. Fully resolve each card's instant effects (except after-finishing effects) before playing the next. Display cards are not refilled until turn end. 4. Instead, Sponsors I advances the Break token by strength and pays that much money even if fewer steps remain. Sponsors II's break option pays twice that amount.
answers.evidence: SPONSORS action sides I and II.

answers.answer: 1. Break order: discard to hand limit (normally 3, or 5 with hand-limit university); clear Multiplier, Venom and Constriction tokens; recall workers and restock eligible partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1–2, compact and refill; take income; reset the Break token. 2. Kiosk income is one money for each adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion. Empty standard enclosures do not qualify; empty special enclosures do. 3. If several players take display cards during break income, resolve them clockwise from the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise from them), and refill after each affected player's income before the next player chooses.
answers.evidence: Break procedure steps 1–6; Kiosk income; display card ordering.

answers.answer: 1. At 2 conservation choose an Action-card upgrade or activate an additional worker. At 5 and 8 choose five money or a Bonus tile at that space; tile is removed after use. At the first time anyone reaches 10, every player discards one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile. If no one reaches 10, all discard one before end scoring. 2. Check the game end at the end of your own turn or during a break when Appeal and Conservation counters are in the same scoring area or pass one another. Appeal gained during someone else's turn waits until your turn end or a break, unless another player triggers the end first. 3. When triggered at a turn end, the triggerer finishes and everyone else gets one more turn; when triggered during a break, everyone gets one more turn. 4. Each Final Scoring card can award at most four conservation points. 5. Victory Points equal Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area occupied by your Conservation counter. Highest positive total wins; ties go to most supported projects, then a shared win.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory Conditions; Final scoring.

answers.answer: 1. Shuffle nine Bonus tiles and randomly place one face up on each of the four blank yellow spaces beside the Conservation track: two beside 5 and two beside 8. Do not put tiles on the two yellow icon spaces; return the other five to the box. 2. The summary says if a component supply runs out, use a suitable substitute; physical stock alone does not prevent a legal play, subject to explicit per-zoo limits and Association-board availability rules.
answers.evidence: Setup global step 2; Special Rules, ‘Component supply’.

answers.answer: 1. For advanced maps, take two random zoo maps and choose one advanced map, or lay out player count plus one advanced maps and choose in reverse turn order; return unselected maps. 2. Map A starts with an empty three-space enclosure and a kiosk on the indicated spaces; the printed kiosk counts as built and a tile is placed over it as a reminder.
answers.evidence: Personal setup A.

answers.answer: 1. The seven conservation-support player tokens begin on the designated spaces at the left edge of your zoo map; taking one to support a project activates its bonus. 2. Hire reserve workers from the lowest supply space upward. 3. Some zoo maps grant a conservation-point reward for hiring your last worker.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C2–C3; Association worker supply special rule.

answers.answer: 1. When you earn an upgrade, flip one chosen Action card from side I to side II; it remains in its current slot. 2. The improved action can be used starting with your next action, but it immediately counts as upgraded for conditions. 3. An upgrade during the current action does not change that action's strength or capabilities. 4. You cannot upgrade all five Action cards; the four upgrade opportunities include one allowing an alternative choice.
answers.evidence: Upgrading Action cards.

answers.answer: 1. At strength 1, Cards I draws 1 and discards 1; strength 2 draws 1 and discards 0; strength 3 draws 2 and discards 1; strength 4 draws 2 and discards 0; strength 5+ draws 3 and discards 1. 2. A required discard may be a card just drawn or one already in your hand.
answers.evidence: Cards draw tables; CARDS action side I.

answers.answer: 1. The seven categories are bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear, and Petting Zoo animal. Bears and Petting Zoo animals count as categories unless explicitly excluded; bear can also appear alongside herbivore or predator.
answers.evidence: Base glossary: shared principles; Animal categories.

answers.answer: 1. Association II permits exactly one donation per Association action, in addition to at least one Association task in that same action. Donation requires no worker. 2. Pay the smallest still-visible amount in the donation area, cover that space with one of your supply player tokens, and gain one conservation point. 3. Printed costs are 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then the repeatable 12-money space; skip spaces blocked at setup. 4. Once every space except the last is covered, each further donation costs 12 money and places no further token.
answers.evidence: ASSOCIATION side II, donation paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. Zoo icons are upper-right icons on Animal and Sponsor cards, partner-zoo and university icons, and upper-left water/rock requirements. Left-side conditions and Conservation Project icons do not count. 2. A card counts its own icons for its effects; doubled icons count twice. 3. Card text takes priority over general rules when they conflict.
answers.evidence: Base glossary shared principles; icon-count projects; ‘Card text takes priority’.

answers.answer: 1. For terrain adjacency, count distinct water or rock hexes that touch the enclosure/building; several touching edges to one hex still count as one. In a larger connected terrain area, count only the hexes actually adjacent. 2. Connected terrain regions do not make all their hexes count as adjacent. 3. Decorative water/rock illustrations on tiles are not terrain spaces and do not fulfill requirements.
answers.evidence: Animal placement terrain rules; Base glossary terrain adjacency.

answers.answer: 1. Only playing a new Release into the Wild project grants one reputation; later support of an existing Release project gives no reputation. 2. Breeding Program projects use the same requirement for all three reward levels; choose any available level that you fulfill, rather than matching a different condition to each space.
answers.evidence: ASSOCIATION release projects; Breeding Program projects.

answers.answer: 1. In an X:Y effect, X is the condition and Y the reward. 2. A condition with no number or with ‘per’ pays once per fulfillment. 3. A numbered threshold pays only once; with multiple thresholds, use the highest one met.
answers.evidence: Base glossary: ‘For an effect written X : Y’.

answers.answer: 1. A connected space is uncovered and shares an edge with a covered space. 2. An isolated space has no adjacent covered space. 3. A border space lacks a neighboring map hex on at least one of its six sides. 4. ‘Your zoo’ includes your played cards, map and personal supply; ‘any zoo’ includes those for all players.
answers.evidence: Base glossary: connected space definitions.

answers.answer: 1. A unique building must be placed when its Sponsor is played; if no legal placement is possible, that Sponsor card cannot be played. 2. Place the matching tile colored face up, freely rotated but not flipped, using ordinary placement and terrain rules. 3. No size-based construction payment is due. 4. Unique buildings are not enclosures, cannot house additional animals and do not count as water or rock spaces.
answers.evidence: Base glossary, unique buildings.

answers.answer: 1. Complete the Animals action and move its card to slot 1 before taking a granted Action. 2. Use the granted Action card normally, then move that card to slot 1 afterward. 3. A named Action cannot be replaced by the X-token alternative; Determination granting any action may choose the X-token alternative.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications, Action / Determination.

answers.answer: 1. Assertion searches the unused face-down base-project deck and adds its chosen project to hand; Dominance adds the named project from that deck. 2. Dominance does nothing if its named project is already in play. 3. Later play and immediately support the acquired card through Association, placing it above the board; it does not enter the base-project row below.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications, Assertion / Dominance.

answers.answer: 1. Resolve Boost and Clever after finishing Animals and moving that Action card. 2. Clever puts its chosen card in slot 1, shifting cards formerly to its left right. 3. Boost puts the named card in slot 1 or slot 5; moving it to slot 5 shifts cards formerly to its right left.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications, Boost / Clever.

answers.answer: 1. All affected zoos must have at least five Appeal for Constriction, Hypnosis, Pilfering or Venom. 2. The playing animal's Appeal may be awarded before or after its ability; normally its new Appeal need not count when selecting the affected players. 3. If the group prefers, interactive abilities can be replaced with the alternative text marked for solo; this does not require playing solo mode.
answers.evidence: Interactive abilities; eligibility and timing.

answers.answer: 1. A target ahead on one track for Constriction gets one token, placed on slot 5; ahead on both Appeal and Conservation gets two, on slots 4 and 5. 2. Never stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates. 3. Each affected action loses two strength, including each execution of a multiplied action; X-tokens can restore strength. 4. Remove the token after using that card, or without effect at the break.
answers.evidence: Interactive target table; Constriction rules.

answers.answer: 1. A Constriction token on a slot-1 or slot-2 card reduces strength by two, potentially to zero or below. To use it, spend enough X-tokens to reach strength at least one, take the alternative X-token action, or leave it until it is at least in slot 3. 2. Thus it cannot perform a regular action at effective strength zero or below, but may take the X-token alternative.
answers.evidence: Constriction rules: effective strength zero or below.

answers.answer: 1. Digging 2 lets you choose up to twice between discarding a display card and replenishing it, or discarding a hand card then drawing one deck card; you may change option after each card. 2. A display card discarded via Digging is replaced immediately, shifting higher folders down and drawing into folder 6.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications, Digging 2.

answers.answer: 1. A flock animal avoids a new enclosure when another herbivore in your zoo requires at least the flock animal's standard-enclosure size. 2. The same qualifying herbivore may host any number of flock animals and need not itself be a flock animal. 3. Without a qualifying herbivore, house the flock animal normally; a later non-flock herbivore cannot join its enclosure. 4. When releasing a flock animal, free an occupied enclosure under the release/fallback procedure; the game does not track historical residents, so no proof of the original accommodation is required.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications, Flock Animal.

answers.answer: 1. Full-throated activates the lowest remaining reserve worker by moving it to the notepad for immediate use. 2. Take any map reward for hiring the last worker, if applicable. 3. If all workers are active, the ability has no effect.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications, Full-throated.

answers.answer: 1. Hunter reveals the specified number of deck cards, adds one revealed Animal card to hand and discards all the other revealed cards. If none is an Animal, discard them all and add no card.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications, Hunter X.

answers.answer: 1. For highest-Appeal ties, choose the target; if you are that target, Hypnosis has no effect. 2. Copy only the target's slot 1, 2 or 3 card, using that card owner's upgraded/unupgraded side for the whole action; other upgrade checks use your own cards. Spend your own X-tokens. 3. Move the copied card to slot 1 normally. 4. Venom and Constriction tokens on it apply to you and are discarded afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used.
answers.evidence: Interactive target reference; Hypnosis rules.

answers.answer: 1. Put a gained Multiplier immediately on its named Action card; a Bonus-tile Multiplier may go on any card. The next use performs that action twice in succession at the same base strength, moving its card only after both executions. 2. Each X-token boosts only one execution. Defer after-finishing effects until both executions are complete. 3. A break triggered by the first execution waits until the whole turn is finished, so it does not stop the second execution. 4. Return used tokens to supply; an unused token is removed at the next break.
answers.evidence: Multiplier rules.

answers.answer: 1. Two Multiplier tokens allow up to three action executions, not four. 2. Each X-token can boost one execution. A multiplied X-token alternative may take two X-tokens subject to the five-token cap, but you cannot mix one X-token action with one regular action.
answers.evidence: Multiplier rules.

answers.answer: 1. Peacocking may place the Large Bird Aviary before Build II, but your zoo must not already have an Aviary and a legal site must exist; other placement restrictions, including Build II for upgrade-marked map spaces, remain. 2. Posturing follows normal placement rules, including kiosk spacing, and multiple buildings are placed one at a time.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications, Peacocking and Posturing.

answers.answer: 1. Petting Zoo animals give 3 Appeal for the first, 6 for the second and 9 for the third. 2. One Petting Zoo holds at most three of these animals. 3. They count as small animals.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications, Petting Zoo animal.

answers.answer: 1. Pilfering 1 selects a highest-Appeal zoo; choose among ties. Pilfering 2 resolves highest-Appeal and most-Conservation targets separately, choosing among ties; the Conservation leader must have at least one conservation point. 2. A self-target has no effect. If one zoo leads both tracks, it may be targeted twice.
answers.evidence: Interactive target reference; Pilfering X rules.

answers.answer: 1. The affected target chooses to give five money or allow a random hand-card draw; Final Scoring cards are never drawn. 2. If the target has no hand cards, it gives five money; if it has less than five money, it gives a card. If it has neither a card nor five money, it gives all current money, including zero. 3. Resolve repeated Pilfering sequentially and allow a different choice each time.
answers.evidence: Pilfering X rules.

answers.answer: 1. Cards tucked under an animal by Pouch have no remaining function; if that animal is released, discard the tucked cards too, but keep the Appeal already earned. 2. Cards sold through Sunbathing go to the discard pile.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications, Pouch X and Sunbathing X.

answers.answer: 1. A Final Scoring card gained through Resistance before the 10-conservation milestone joins the cards from which you choose one to discard at that milestone. 2. At game end score every remaining Final Scoring card, each subject to its own maximum of four conservation points.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications, Resistance.

answers.answer: 1. For Scavenging, shuffle the discard pile face down, draw randomly from it, make the card's stated selection, then return the discard pile face up. For the illustrated Scavenging 3, draw three random cards, keep one and discard the others.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications, Scavenging.

answers.answer: 1. Snapping takes exactly one display card regardless of reputation; it does not draw from the deck. Sponsor Magnet selects display Sponsors regardless of reputation range; if there is no Sponsor in the display, it has no effect. 2. Ordinary end-of-turn display refill applies.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications, Snapping and Sponsor Magnet.

answers.answer: 1. Put Venom tokens on cards in the lowest slots first (slot 1, then 2, etc.), at most one per card; return duplicates to supply. 2. Using a card with Venom removes its token and avoids all Venom fees that turn, including when using it for the X-token alternative if you hold fewer than five X-tokens. 3. At turn end, pay two money only if you removed no Venom token that turn and at least one Venom token remains on your cards. If you cannot pay, undo the turn and choose a different action; spending all money does not avoid it. 4. The next break clears unused tokens without effect.
answers.evidence: Venom rules.

answers.answer: 1. Veterinarian gives 2, 5 or 10 money immediately for having 1, 2 or 3 universities respectively. 2. Its recurring effect reduces Conservation Project support task strength from 5 to 4. 3. Its final reward is one conservation point for three universities.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 203 Veterinarian.

answers.answer: 1. Medical Breakthrough gives two Appeal per previously supported project, counted as player tokens missing from the left edge of your zoo map. 2. It gives one conservation point in every break.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 206 Medical Breakthrough.

answers.answer: 1. Basic Research counts different continent and animal-category icons; it gives one conservation per two such icons. 2. Each other player gets two money per conservation point you gain.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 207 Basic Research.

answers.answer: 1. Science Library gives one Appeal per research icon immediately. 2. Whenever any player plays a research icon, the Science Library owner—not necessarily the player who played it—gets two money. 3. Its final condition grants one conservation for five different animal categories.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 208 Science Library.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on the Americas gives one Appeal per Americas icon immediately. 2. Each Americas icon played permits a free kiosk under normal placement rules, including spacing. 3. Its final condition is one conservation with five or more kiosks.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 210 Expert on the Americas.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on Australia gives one Appeal per Australia icon immediately. 2. For each Australia icon played, you may tuck one hand card beneath the Sponsor for two Appeal. 3. Tucked cards have no further function.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 212 Expert on Australia.

answers.answer: 1. Global Breeding Program and Breeding Program put two supply tokens on the Sponsor when played. When supporting a base project below the Association board, return exactly one token as any one icon; never use both for one support. 2. Base-origin cards played above the board do not qualify. 3. Their final reward is one conservation for five or more project supports, counted by missing left-map tokens.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 215/218.

answers.answer: 1. Engineer allows each Build action to add one extra copy of a building built in that same action, without additional strength. Pay its normal money cost and obey placement rules. 2. Only one extra building is allowed even if several different buildings are built; two identical buildings otherwise cannot be built in a single Build II action, and special enclosures retain their one-per-type-per-zoo limit. 3. Its final reward is five Appeal with a full map except water/rock.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 217 Engineer; Build II limits.

answers.answer: 1. Diversity Researcher gives one Appeal per water/rock icon immediately. 2. It lets you cover water/rock spaces and ignore terrain requirements of animals and unique buildings; printed terrain icons still count. 3. Covered terrain stops counting for Hydrologist, Geologist and Architectural Zoo; terrain need not be covered to score a full map. 4. It scores two Appeal per water-icon/rock-icon pair, up to three pairs.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 219 Diversity Researcher.

answers.answer: 1. Each actual placement bonus on a border space triggers Archaeologist's additional choice of any uncovered placement bonus on your map, not necessarily one on the border. 2. Multiple border-space bonuses allow multiple extra choices, and copied bonuses may be the same or different; resolve in chosen order. 3. Its final condition grants one conservation when all building border spaces are covered, excluding water/rock.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 221 Archaeologist.

answers.answer: 1. Migration Recording gives one X-token immediately. 2. Each Release into the Wild support gives one additional conservation. 3. You may repeatedly support the same release project with different qualifying animals, but place at most one token on that project per Association action. 4. Each token counts as a separate project support for other effects.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 224 Migration Recording.

answers.answer: 1. Quarantine Lab gives one X-token immediately. 2. It makes you immune to Venom, Constriction, Hypnosis and Pilfering. For Hypnosis and Pilfering, ignore your counters and select the next qualifying player. 3. Its final condition grants one conservation with all five continents.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 225 Quarantine Lab.

answers.answer: 1. Choose small or large permanently, mark that choice with a supply player token, and reveal deck cards until an animal of that chosen size type appears; keep it and discard the others. 2. You cannot play the opposite type. 3. Chosen small animals give two extra Appeal; chosen large animals give four. Size-3 animals remain legal but earn no bonus. Small means printed standard size 1 or 2, including Petting Zoo animals; large means size 4 or 5.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 227 WAZA Special Assignment; size definitions.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Small Animals Program gives two money per small animal immediately. 2. If an Animals action contains only small animals, you may play one extra small animal from hand, paying normal costs and following normal rules. 3. Then add one small animal from the display to hand regardless of reputation; you may take this display animal even if you declined the extra play. Mixing small and large animals in the original action prevents the effect.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 228 WAZA Small Animals Program.

answers.answer: 1. Hydrologist gives one Appeal per water icon immediately. 2. Its recurring money effect gives one money for each newly covered space adjacent to water, even multiple spaces within one building; a space beside several water hexes pays only once. 3. Its final reward is one conservation if all water hexes are connected, meaning none is isolated.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 241 Hydrologist.

answers.answer: 1. Barred Owl Hut is a unique building that must be placed when its Sponsor is played, subject to ordinary placement rules. 2. Each bird icon played triggers drawing two deck cards, keeping one and discarding the other.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 249 Barred Owl Hut; unique buildings.

answers.answer: 1. Sea Turtle Tank is a unique building placed adjacent to water. 2. Each reptile icon played lets you sell up to two hand cards for four money each; sold cards are discarded.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 250 Sea Turtle Tank.

answers.answer: 1. Spotted Hyena Compound must be placed adjacent to rock. Each predator icon played triggers Hunter with draws equal to your total predator icons. 2. If a newly played card has two predator icons, resolve two Hunters sequentially, counting both new icons each time.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 252 Spotted Hyena Compound.

answers.answer: 1. Okapi Stable is placed as a unique building with three supply tokens on its card. 2. For each herbivore icon played, you may spend one token to play a Sponsor from hand, following normal conditions, and receive money equal to that Sponsor's level. 3. Its own herbivore icon can trigger this when the Stable is played; three uses total.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 253 Okapi Stable.

answers.answer: 1. Zoo School immediately gives one reputation and one conservation. 2. Place its unique building covering at least two border spaces. 3. Take one display card within reputation range or draw one from the deck. Resolve its simultaneous benefits in the order you choose.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 254 Zoo School.

answers.answer: 1. Side Entrance is placed on two border spaces and, unlike ordinary buildings, need not touch an existing building; ordinary placement rules still apply, and later buildings may attach to it. 2. In each break it gives two money per adjacent building except empty standard enclosures; it may be adjacent to a kiosk. 3. Its final reward is five Appeal with a full map excluding water/rock.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 257 Side Entrance.

answers.answer: 1. Native Farm Animals immediately gives one Appeal per connected uncovered building-border space; water/rock spaces do not count. 2. At game end it gives one conservation per six contiguous empty building spaces, evaluated separately for each group (for example groups of 13, 6, 3 and 2 yield 2+1+0+0=3). 3. Upgrade-restricted spaces count even if Build is not upgraded; water/rock spaces are excluded.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 260 Native Farm Animals.

answers.answer: 1. Explorer immediately gives two money per different continent/animal-category icon; research icons do not count. 2. Each category or continent newly introduced to your zoo gives one Appeal and two money. A newly played double of the same new icon grants this novelty benefit only once.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 262 Explorer.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Large Animal Program lets you place a size-5 standard enclosure free under normal placement rules. 2. Its recurring effect lets you ignore one left-side condition when playing a large animal; terrain requirements cannot be ignored. 3. It stacks with Research Institute, which can ignore one additional condition, for two conditions total.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 263 WAZA Large Animal Program; Map 6 Research Institute.

answers.answer: 1. Biodiverse Zoo compares your animal-category icon count against the player to your right and grants one conservation for each category where your count is greater. 2. If the neighbor has none of a category, one of your icons is enough. 3. The reward is capped at four conservation.
answers.evidence: Base Final Scoring and map clarifications, Biodiverse Zoo (009).

answers.answer: 1. Observation Tower benefits only standard enclosures adjacent to the tower hex itself, not enclosures merely adjacent to another rock hex. 2. Special enclosures do not qualify; the Tower is not a building for kiosk income. 3. Housing an animal there grants its two Appeal again even if an earlier animal was released and the enclosure was emptied.
answers.evidence: Map 1, Observation Tower.

answers.answer: 1. Outdoor Areas applies to a standard enclosure touching the Outdoor Area hex itself, not merely another water hex. 2. It counts as two spaces larger for all purposes after placement; a physical size-2 enclosure is treated as size 4. 3. The increase cannot be ignored for release or transfer. 4. It does not affect special enclosures, and Outdoor Areas is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 2, Outdoor Areas.

answers.answer: 1. A building on Commercial Harbor's adjacent building space activates it; the first building may start beside the Harbor but need not. 2. Its discard ability may be used before, during or after your action, once per own turn, never during breaks or another player's turn. 3. The Harbor is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 4, Commercial Harbor.

answers.answer: 1. Park Restaurant break income is one money per adjacent covered hex, regardless of building type, occupancy or whether several hexes belong to one building; empty enclosures qualify. 2. The Restaurant is not itself a building and does not count for kiosk income. 3. Its special-enclosure placement bonus gives one free Reptile House or one free Large Bird Aviary, even before Build II; choose one, not both, and follow all other ordinary placement rules.
answers.evidence: Map 5, Park Restaurant.

answers.answer: 1. Cover each Hollywood Hills H space with a building following ordinary placement rules. When each H is covered, reveal cards from the deck until a Sponsor appears; keep it and discard the rest. 2. H is not a placement bonus and does not trigger Archaeologist. 3. After all three are covered, every Sponsor's level is one lower. 4. Its bonus partner zoos still require Association II for the third/fourth partner, and bonus buildings still require Build II for upgrade-marked spaces.
answers.evidence: Map 8, Hollywood Hills.

answers.answer: 1. Pay money equal to the Sponsor's level and meet its usual play conditions. 2. This bonus permits playing the Sponsor only from hand, even with Sponsors II; it cannot come from the display. 3. The Sponsors Action card stays in its current slot and does not move.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ, paid Sponsor bonus.

answers.answer: 1. Appeal cannot exceed 113 and conservation cannot exceed 41; gains beyond either track end are lost. 2. Reputation has a separate overflow rule: at space 15, each further reputation step becomes one Appeal.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ, bonus icons and track caps; Reputation track.

answers.answer: 1. Venom affects every other zoo with higher Appeal than yours, subject to the five-Appeal minimum. 2. Hypnosis targets a highest-Appeal zoo with at least five Appeal; choose a tie, and if you are the target it has no effect; copy only slot 1, 2 or 3. 3. Pilfering 1 targets a highest-Appeal zoo; Pilfering 2 resolves highest Appeal and most Conservation separately, each requiring five Appeal and at least one Conservation for the latter; choose ties, and self-targeting has no effect. 4. Constriction affects every other zoo with at least five Appeal that is ahead on Appeal and/or Conservation: one lead gives one token on slot 5; leads on both give two tokens on slots 4 and 5.
answers.evidence: Interactive abilities eligibility; Interactive target reference.

answers.answer: 1. For an Animal card's partner-zoo condition, the partner must be from that animal's continent. A Sponsor card's partner-zoo condition can be met by any continent. 2. A red maximum-25 Appeal condition means play only while your zoo has at most 25 Appeal; 25 is a reminder, not a general track cap. 3. A minimum-reputation condition requires at least its printed reputation. 4. An ignore-one-condition bonus removes one left-side card condition, not a terrain requirement.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ, condition clarifications; Diversity/condition rules.

answers.answer: 1. Crested Porcupine's Digging 2 permits up to two selections, each choosing either discard a display card and replenish it or discard a hand card and draw one deck card. 2. You may choose either option separately each time; display discards refill immediately, shifting higher folders down and drawing into folder 6.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications, Digging 2.

answers.answer: 1. After display cards are taken in a turn, move higher-numbered folder cards down in their order, then fill empty spaces from the deck; refill only at turn end. 2. During breaks discard folders 1 and 2, move remaining cards down, then refill. 3. For between-player break-income display picks, refill after each affected player's income before the next player chooses. (Digging specifically replaces a discarded display card immediately.)
answers.evidence: CARDS action display refill; Break procedure; Digging 2.

answers.answer: 1. Build a standard enclosure with its empty side up, showing yellow border and size number. 2. Each placement-bonus icon on a covered space is awarded immediately once; resolve all such bonuses before placing the next building. Turning the enclosure occupied later does not award the bonus again.
answers.evidence: BUILD action opening paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. When the first player reaches or exceeds 10 conservation, each player discards one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining Final Scoring pile. The summary specifies face down and under the pile; it does not state a separate rotation/orientation beyond that.
answers.evidence: Scoring, Conservation track 10: ‘discard one ... (face down under the remaining pile)’.

answers.answer: 1. Randomly determine the starting player; thereafter turns proceed clockwise. The game has no formal rounds: players take turns one at a time until an end condition. 2. On a turn you perform one action using one of the five Action cards. Additional ‘after finishing’ effects or permitted effects granted by cards may resolve after that action; the normal turn action count remains one.
answers.evidence: Setup, global step 7; Overview; Turn Structure.
